collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A water channel would help most families but cut through two family gardens: build it and make it up to them, or route it around.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A new water channel would bring water to twenty gardens. The only straight path runs through the gardens of (friend)'s family and one other. (subject) says the many outweigh the few. (friend) says (friend.his/her) grandmother planted that garden. What should the village decide?

choices.label: Build It and Make It Up

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The channel is built. The two families are given new gardens and help to plant them. (friend) accepts, stiffly. The channel waters the whole village. (friend) still walks past the old garden every morning.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The channel winds around the two gardens, which makes it twice as long and takes a whole season more. The other families grumble about the wait. (friend)'s grandmother's garden stays where it is.
